_source: Jagatjit Agri Engineering Limited DRHP dated 25-Sep-2026 (SEBI filing 01-Oct-2026). Rs crore = Rs million / 10. Printed page = PDF page - 6. Restated financials: FY26 consolidated, FY24 and FY25 standalone (the subsidiary was acquired after FY25); the businesses of two promoter proprietorships were acquired with effect from 1-Apr-2025, so FY24-FY25 restated figures are not like-for-like with FY26. Proforma figures (pp. 91-92) are in the note. Related-party rows include the two acquired proprietorships (Saron Mechanical Works I and II) for FY24-FY25.

cites.nw: p. 85 (total equity; ICDR net worth p. 155)

1.finding: 22:1 bonus (allotted 27-May-2026) and a 1:2 split are applied to EPS and NAV for all years (EPS 5.64 / 1.42 / 0.57; NAV Rs 12.75 on 55,650,984 shares). The FY26 balance sheet share capital of Rs 12.10 m is the pre-bonus count of 1,209,804 shares of Rs 10 (p. 85); post-bonus and split there are 55,650,984 shares of Rs 5 (p. 112). Presentation point only.

2.finding: CFO positive in all three years: Rs 124.93 m / 130.15 m / 26.85 m (FY24/25/26); cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7% (281.93 / 404.39), on mixed standalone and consolidated bases. FY26 CFO/PAT 8.6%: CFO before working capital was Rs 619.53 m, inventory absorbed Rs 445.46 m and other assets Rs 281.35 m. CFO is struck before interest of Rs 101.63 m in FY26.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 130.30 m on PBT of Rs 444.12 m = 29.3% in FY26 (statutory 25.17%); deferred tax is a credit of Rs 0.09 m. Cumulative current tax / PBT 26.1% over FY24-26 (147.09 / 562.64).

4.finding: Business transfer agreements dated 27-Aug-2025 bought two promoter proprietorships (Rs 69.13 m from Dharam Singh, Rs 255.44 m from Jagatjit Singh) for shares at Rs 1,547 pre-bonus and pre-split (about Rs 33.63 per Rs 5 share), on a single registered valuer's report. The proposed Rs 716.64 m expansion is on 16.20 acres leased from Jagatjit Singh at Rs 0.08 m per month, +15% every three years (p. 129). Related-party loans and advances to promoters outstanding: Rs 45.00 m (Jagatjit Singh) and Rs 10.00 m (Dharam Singh) at 31-Mar-2026 (p. 95).

5.finding: Fresh issue is amount-based (Rs 3,000 m), so no fixed share count and no objects price floor. Identified objects total Rs 2,001.64 m (66.7%); the balance of about Rs 998.4 m is general corporate purposes (stated cap 25% of gross proceeds, Rs 750 m) and offer expenses.

6.finding: No revaluation reserve line in the restated balance sheet.

7.finding: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m at 31-Mar-2026 against tangible net worth Rs 704.74 m. The proforma balance sheet at 31-Mar-2025 shows goodwill of Rs 65.66 m (p. 91) and a capital reserve of Rs 32.98 m at 31-Mar-2024; the restated FY26 balance sheet carries Rs 4.55 m. The DRHP does not reconcile the two treatments of the same acquisitions.

8.finding: FY26 top customer 25.21%, top 5 40.84%, top 10 50.04% of revenue; in FY25 the top customer (21.86%) was one of the acquired proprietorships. Top supplier 7.94%, top 10 40.53% of raw material purchases in FY26 (76.68% and 96.69% in FY25 and FY24 on restated basis). No long-term supply agreements (p. 23). Top three products (Super Seeder, Straw Reaper, Laser Land Leveller) = 64.40% of FY26 revenue (p. 450). Demand for flagship products depends on CRM and SMAM subsidy schemes (p. 56).

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 71.70 m (income tax 0.18, GST 22.67, other 6.50, bank guarantees 42.35) = 10.1% of ICDR net worth of Rs 709.29 m. Litigation materiality threshold is the lowest of three tests, Rs 6.74 m (p. 488).

R1.finding: No qualification or emphasis of matter requiring adjustment (p. 344). Statutory auditor Anup Kumar Jain & Co. appointed 30-Sep-2024 on completion of the previous auditor's tenure (p. 98). Audit trail: accounting software of the parent had no database-level audit trail up to December 2025 (p. 343).

R2.finding: CARO 2020 audit trail: feature not enabled at database level for the parent company's accounting software up to December 2025. No adjustment to restated numbers.

R3.finding: The company will appoint a monitoring agency before the RHP is filed (pp. 101, 152). Debt repayment object is Rs 185.00 m of borrowings not yet identified by lender. Directors Jagatjit Singh and Dharam Singh were appointed on 29-Sep-2020 while disqualified under the Companies Act (the DRHP states the disqualification subsisted to 31-Oct-2021); an adjudication application was filed on 11-Sep-2026 and is pending (p. 489). Personal guarantees and promoter property security for the borrowings were not tested in this screen.

R4.finding: Issue is made under Reg 6(2): not less than 75% of the Net Offer to QIBs because net tangible assets and net worth tests of Reg 6(1)(a) and 6(1)(c) are not met for the preceding three years. KPI EBITDA Rs 557.38 m reproduces from the P&L (PBT 444.12 + finance 101.63 + D&A 46.66 - other income 35.03). Total assets and total liabilities reproduce at Rs 3,188.36 m.

R5.finding: Offer for sale of 3,100,000 shares by Jagatjit Singh, 6.3% of his 48,990,736 shares; about Rs 49.1 m at the Rs 158.48 reference = 14.1% of the Rs 3,000 m fresh issue. Test any OFS ceiling against the ICDR as in force when the RHP fixes the price.

R6.finding: DRHP gives two issues by Keynote Financial Services (Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (Exports) and CSM Technologies) with 30/90-day moves; both recorded in data/merchant_bankers.json. The BRLM's full track record is delegated to its website (p. 512). Current prices and issuer financials not compiled.

R7.finding: Whether the Rs 3,000 m fresh issue needs a separate means-of-finance tie-up beyond the Rs 2,001.64 m identified objects is not stated; general corporate purposes and offer expenses are left blank in the DRHP.

rationale.g1: Proforma revenue Rs 2,074.48 m / 2,537.60 m / 4,139.70 m FY24-26: +22.3% then +63.1% (pp. 91-92, 87); units sold 8,895 / 12,234 / 19,111 (p. 158). FY26 growth is unit-led (+56.2%) with revenue per unit +4.4%. Bear assumes the subsidy-led volume step does not repeat (top three products 64.4% of revenue, p. 450; CRM and SMAM scheme risk, p. 56); Bull assumes 18-state reach (p. 158) and the Dehlon expansion lift volume.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 9.74% / 14.51% / 13.46% proforma FY24, proforma FY25, FY26 (p. 158). Bear sits just above the FY24 proforma level; Bull is above the FY25 high. Margin moved because gross margin rose to 39.06% while other expenses rose to 18.94% of revenue (pp. 87, 158).
rationale.nwc: Trade working capital (inventory + receivables - payables) is 20.3% of FY26 revenue (Rs 838.52 m, p. 85) and 21.4% on proforma FY25 (Rs 544.01 m on payables of Rs 568.51 m, pp. 91, 126). Inventory days 132, receivable days 45, payable days 106 in FY26 (p. 128).
rationale.roic: Issuer-defined ROCE 31.10% FY26 and 31.55% proforma FY25 (p. 158) on a book base that includes assets acquired from promoters at agreed value. Terminal ROIC set well below this and near the 15% to 25% range because the FY26 base is a single consolidated year.
